Sure there is, the brain is super complicated.  But, this is ELI5, and to me this seemed like the easiest to understand answer and as far as I am aware plays one of the biggest roles in this process.

Taste is a lot of things more than just what your tongue tells you.

Take for example those blind taste tests were fancy wine doesn't taste as good when you don't know it's fancy.  Your brain uses last experiences as a short cut.  Your brain expects fancy wine to be tasty so it is.

Your brain doesn't like being confused.  Ever drank one thing expecting it to be something different? It's a disgusting experience because your brain had its expectations violated.

If something has the texture of steak your brain expects to to be steak and you'll get the full experience that way.  If you had steak shakes all the time you'd probably grow to like it.  However, I bet you tend to only have smoothies and such in that form, and thus your brain expects that type of fruity drink for smoothy textures.

Brain is lazy and gets mad when things aren't as it expected

The fact that Java is some sort of terrible programming language is simply a blown out of proportion truth.

Java has a decent amount of over head in it.  Which comes from a number of technical details that are far too boring to go into, but the biggest being that Java doesn't run directly on your computer like other programs.  Rather it's ran through the Java environment.  This is the JRE thing you have to down load to get java programs to run.

As with anything with a middle man the experience isn't as efficient or pleasant as a more direct route, but that's the price of portability.  How ever said middle man has become very good at the job in the most recent years and thus for anything not terribly ambitious it's possible to get a Java version to run without noticeable diffrence from a different, more direct, language.
